steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Make the crust: Combine flour, brown sugar, and softened butter in a large mixer bowl. Beat at medium speed until mixture resembles fine crumbs, 2 to 3 minutes. Transfer mixture to an ungreased 13x9-inch baking pan. Pat evenly over the bottom to form a crust.

Make the turtle layer: Combine butter and brown sugar in small saucepan over medium heat. Cook and stir until bubbles form over the entire surface. Continue to cook, stirring constantly, 30 to 60 seconds more. Remove from the heat.
Sprinkle pecans evenly over the crust, then pour hot brown sugar mixture over top.
Bake in the preheated oven until the entire surface is bubbly, 18 to 20 minutes.

Remove from the oven and set on a wire rack. Immediately sprinkle chocolate chips evenly over the surface and let stand until chocolate melts, 2 to 3 minutes. Use a knife or small spatula to swirl the melted chocolate slightly.
Let sit until completely cooled, about 30 minutes. Use a sharp knife to cut into 48 bars.

raw_recipe.headline: Pecan Turtles Bars
raw_recipe.description: Follow this recipe for quick and easy pecan turtle bars and you'll have a treat that both adults and kids will love.
raw_recipe.name: Pecan Turtles Bars

review.reviewBody: These are one of my favorite bars! I do the topping a little differently though. When I make them I double the butter and sugar mixture for the topping. Another reviewer said there wasn't enough to cover the bars but this solves the problem and its the best part of the bars anyway.

Doubled recipe, baked in jelly roll pan for 25minutes. Did not have brown sugar so for doubled recipe used 3cups white sugar AND 1cup molasses (total). Lined pan with aluminum foil then lined that pan with parchmant paper; was very easy to remove and slice after they were cooled. Will make again! Thank you, Marlyn.

Did as many here suggested and doubled the flour mixture and they came out great! I also did the Sweetened Condensed Milk caramel (a can of SCM in its can (with label off),covered in water and cooked in a crockpot for 8 hours)thinned out with some milk and it worked beautifully, though I may do 2 cans next time.

These are super rich so a small bar suffices :)

My son had these bars from a local bakery so I decided to make some at home, don't get me wrong these taste awesome, but as written the squares would not work. I halved the recipe for a 9x9 pan, used 1 cup flour, 1/4 cup brown sugar and 1/2 cup of butter for the base. I used my hands to make the base and pressed down hard with my potato masher. For the topping I used 1/2 cup ground pecans as that is what I had leftover from Christmas baking with 1/4 cup brown sugar, 1/3 cup butter and 1 tsp vanilla added after boiling. I used semi sweet chips, didn't measure just sprinkled over the top, then swirled when melted. I wish the submitter or Allrecipes would add divided in the ingredients for the brown sugar and butter because if you don't read the recipe through properly you would not know you need it for the base and topping until it was too late. I also lined my pan with parchment paper for easy removal and clean up. Next time make the full recipe for the 9x9 pan to make them thicker.

These were very yummy. I do have some suggestions. I also upped the flour as suggested to 2 cups. I doubled the caramel middle layers as well and think that really is necessary. Some reviewers are complaining about a "buttery mess" or butter leaking out the top. If you are not combining the caramel layer well, I can see this would happen. I mixed the caramel with a silicone whisk to make sure it was totally blended. I would also melt the chocolate and pour it over rather than sprinkle on the chips and try to spread them. Much neater presentation that way and you assured the chocolate melts.

These bars are amazing. Served them to 4 adults and 2/3 of the pan were gone!
I did use 2 cups of flour, doubled the caramel layer and used 2 cups milk chocolate chips. After baking it, I let it cool, then I melted the chocolate in the microwave and poured on top which made it much easier to spread. This should be allowed to cool for a few hours in order to set properly, which made it easier to cut and less "oozy".
Would absolutely make it again, and again!

Love these! Every time I make them they get devoured. I double the caramel part of the recipe & sprinkle flaked coconut on the crust before adding the caramel and baking. It tastes good with milk, semi-sweet & cinnamon chocolate chips.

I added 1/2 cup pecans in order to better cover the bottom layer. Also could NOT get the chocolate chips to melt after taking them out of the oven and waiting a few minutes so I put them back in at warm (150 degrees) for another 20 minutes. When the chips still didn't melt or spread, I went and bought another package of milk chocolate chips and melted in the microwave per the package instructions then spread the entire 11.5 ounces on top. They tasted good (although a little dry after additional time in the oven) but if I make again, I will definitely use a whole bag of chocolate chips and melt in the microwave along with extra pecans.

Great recipe. I think missing a little salt, am making again today and will add it. Also will chop the pecan halves some to make them a bit smaller. Added tip: After removing from the oven and adding the chocolate chips, I put a cookie sheet over the top to hold the heat in and that assists in melting the chocolate.

These are indeed some yummy treats! I think if it were my recipe though, I'd name it Pecan TOFFEE Bars. I did make changes per reviews. I doubled middle filling, when doin' so, cut back butter by 1/4 cup...so only use 3/4 cup for double middle filling. I did add extra 1/2 cup of flour to crust, it seems like it'll be too dry at first, but it'll soak up some butter from the filling...mine did. I doubled the chocolate, BUT, next time I won't, it detracts the great flavor from the filling. Also, I will wait until the pan is cooled from the oven and I will premelt and drizzle the chocolate over decoratively. I also used almonds along with pecans, next time I will add extra, I'm nutty and love nutty :P

These were pretty yummy. However they were quite greasy, butter was oozing up between the chocolate. The caramel mixture should be equal parts butter and brown sugar, 1/2 c butter instead of 2/3 c. And next time I will double the caramel:) One other problem I has was I couldn't get the milk choc chips to melt enough to spread. Semisweet chips melt and spread much better, so I would recommend using those instead, and increase the amount to 1&1/2 c. I will make these again!

I modified these to be gluten free, using 2 cups of almond flour instead of 1 1/2 cups normal flour. I doubled the caramel filling, and had to use 2 1/2 cups of chocolate to cover the pan. After baking, the butter separated from the filling and rose to the top. Even after coating with chocolate, the butter was still separated. I scooped some of the butter off with a spoon, and tried to absorb it with paper towels, but there was so much on the top. Once cooled, you could still see the stripes of the butter. It tasted delicious, but this recipe needs help.
I regret making this 😭 the caramel soaked into the biscuit so there are no layers
Perfect! They always come out amazing!
Sampled a few as soon it was done cooling down. But I’m sure will be better and less messy after refrigeration.

Ridiculously simple and so very delicious. Can recommend substituting in dark chocolate chips for the milk chocolate on top, it will still melt just fine and adds a stronger chocolate flavor. You can put the pan in the freezer for half an hour if the bars are taking a while to set after baking. Will be making these in the future for any occasion.
fabulous

I added a little more pecans and a little more chocolate to cover the bottom. Tasted very good and sweet! I just don't have the right technique of swirling the chocolate. Not that pretty but an excellent treat!

Too many adjustments because the recipe as written does not work. I did all the adjustments even put the chocolate chips on 10 minutes before the recipe was done. What a disaster. The chocolate chips never melted. Took over two hours and it is a complete mess. And I tripled it for gifting. Very disappointed.
I made these last year and they will be a regular from here on. These are a hit with very little effort.
